identification.offer_type_hint: Year-round program = continuous availability. Seasonal = narrow window. Promo listing = one-off listing with a better price. Spot = production surplus.
identification.positioning_label: Role of the product on the shelf
identification.positioning_hint: Everyday = mainstream. Premium = higher price and quality. Promo = low price with label. Bio = certified. Local = from retailer's country. Shelf-ready = in RSP packaging.

quality_spec.info_alert_html: Fields in this section are optional — fill them in only if relevant to your product and the buyer. We focus on the basic specification; commercial details will be agreed after contact.
quality_spec.size_placeholder: e.g. apples 70-80 mm · blueberries 12+ mm · citrus 6 (cal.) · roses 50-60 cm
quality_spec.size_hint: Industry standard or the measure you use to indicate product size.
quality_spec.quality_class_hint: Class I = EU standard (most of trade). Extra = top EU. Premium/A = retailer's own classes. Other = industry certifications (e.g. GlobalGAP grade).
quality_spec.quality_spec_placeholder: uniform caliber, good firmness, no mechanical damage, stable batch throughout the program
quality_spec.bio_toggle_label: Product has an organic / Bio certificate

flowers.opening_phase_hint: Flower development stage at harvest. You can enter the value in your own words.
flowers.flower_color_placeholder: e.g. red, spring mix, white and pink

photos.info_alert: The first photo (main) goes into the header of the buyer's email. A photo of the trade packaging is required — the buyer and logistics must see exactly what they get.
photos.uploader_label: Click or drag product photos here
photos.hint: The first photo will be the main one in the buyer's email. Photos are stored in the cloud and visible to all users.

availability.model_hint: Year-round = stable delivery 12 months. Seasonal = product in a defined window (e.g. strawberries V-VII). Short window = a few weeks. Spot = one-off batch, no continuation.
availability.promo_vol_label: Can the volume be increased for promo?

packaging.success_alert: The buyer and warehouse assess whether the product can be implemented before the conversation begins. Pallet dimensions, carton counts and SRP are often entry conditions.
packaging.custom_packaging_hint: e.g. Big Bag, Mesh Bag, Tray, Sleeve...
packaging.desc_placeholder: e.g. 12 x 125 g, 10 kg bulk, 20 bunches of 10 pcs.

logistics.regions_placeholder: e.g. PL, DE, CZ, NL — all of CEE
logistics.transport_hint: Indicate who organizes transport. It can be your company, a courier company or the buyer.
logistics.temp_hint: optional — often depends on the route

commercial.card_title: E. Commercial terms and indicative price
commercial.info_alert_html: Price is optional and indicative. Preconnect is a system for product proposals, not classic price quoting. You can list an indicative price, a range, or leave the field empty — the buyer will ask for the price after contact. Any price shown to the buyer will include the note: “Price is indicative and requires confirmation from the supplier.”
commercial.price_placeholder: e.g. 2.40 — min. price from the previous week
commercial.price_hint: Optional. Shows the buyer the order of magnitude — the final price will be agreed bilaterally. INCOTERMS impact: DAP/DDP usually higher, EXW lower.

step3.warning_alert_html:
Don't write: high quality · competitive price · individual approach · many years of experience.
Be specific: batch standard, volume, logistics, price, response time, benefit for the buyer.

example.summary: 📋 Show an example of a good proposal (1 sentence)
example.quote: “Gala apples 70-80 mm, class I, 100 t/month, DAP delivery to distribution center”
example.explanation_html: Every field is specific and measurable: product + variety + caliber + class + volume + logistics. The buyer immediately knows what to expect. Keep the same spirit in the 3 questions below — operational, in numbers.

benefits.success_alert_html: This is the most important section — more important than price. Answer the 3 questions specifically: why should the buyer choose your proposal? Don't write clichés — write operational, measurable facts.
benefits.q1: Why should the buyer be interested in this product?
benefits.q1_placeholder: e.g. repeatable batch quality throughout the program — optical sorter, class I guaranteed
benefits.q2: What do you do better or differently than other suppliers?
benefits.q2_placeholder: e.g. stable supply of 200–500 t/month from our own CA cold storage — independent of purchase market
benefits.q3: How do you reduce risk for the buyer?
benefits.q3_placeholder: e.g. claims handled the same day, plan B: 2 packhouses + 5 partner farms
benefits.shop_benefit_label: How will this product help the retailer sell more or better?
benefits.shop_benefit_placeholder: shelf-friendly format, low waste, room for a seasonal campaign, POS material support, ready for display

risk.mitigation_label: How do you safeguard quality and supply continuity?
risk.mitigation_placeholder: batch quality monitoring, same-day claim response, full traceability from field to delivery, online documentation, contingency plan: 2 packhouses + 5 partner farms
risk.proof_placeholder: markets served: PL/DE/CZ, stable volumes since 2019, retail references (on request), process photos, current GlobalGAP tests
risk.now_label: Why is it worth talking now?
risk.now_placeholder: e.g. start of autumn season — Class Extra apples available from September, high availability from CA cold storage, window before holiday promo

actions.info_alert_html: Note: actions are on the buyer's side. The buyer decides what to do after reviewing your proposal. They can request a sample, ask about current price and volume, request a specification, schedule a call, ask about a seasonal program, or arrange a meeting at Fresh Market. They can also contact you directly using the contact details provided in your profile.

title_card.info_alert_html: This is your proposal title visible to the buyer on the proposal list. It should immediately tell what you offer and why it's worth clicking for details. Enter the product, country or region of origin, and one strongest differentiator — e.g. season, caliber, availability, certification, or packaging format.
title_card.title_placeholder: e.g. Table grapes Murcia — seedless, AA caliber, season VII–X
title_card.internal_title_placeholder: e.g. Gala premium — variant for large retailers
title_card.internal_title_description: This is a working name just for you. The buyer won't see it. Use it to easily distinguish similar proposals in your panel — e.g. a variant for large retailers, a seasonal proposal, or a premium variant.
